Stanza 10 has no supplied photo or caption; its scene derives from canonical Sanskrit alone. Portrait production is paused.

rows.scene: Bali is restored by Shukra’s rite and rules with power; distant Devas withdraw in fear. Keep the prior battle implied, not graphic.
rows.candidate_status: Producer uncertain: the side-on Bali foot has only three clear toe separations and Deva prayer digits overlap; five-toe anatomy and individual prayer digits are not fully countable. Skin-only human samples range R-B 62–122; Shukra’s upper arm is 122 but reads warm brown. Prior independent review passed this exact checksum against the earlier plan. Final-plan independent review is pending.

rows.scene: Aditi grieves for her sons and seeks Kashyapa’s help; he instructs the twelve-day milk vow and worship.
rows.candidate_status: Producer pass: Aditi and Kashyapa are distinct and naturally posed; sampled face R-B values are 128 and 114 and both read brown, not orange. Aditi’s prayer hands overlap in the pose but show no malformed digits; Kashyapa’s teaching hand is coherent. Prior independent review passed this exact checksum against the earlier plan. Final-plan independent review is pending.

rows.scene: After the vow, the dark blue four-armed Lord appears before Aditi and tells her he will be born as her son. Exactly four attached arms.
rows.candidate_status: Producer pass: Vishnu has exactly four attached arms, three distinct attributes and a clear blessing palm with thumb plus four fingers; both feet show five toes. Vishnu skin-only samples measure B−R 61; Aditi cheek/forearm patches measure R−B 86/95 and read muted brown. Final-plan independent review is pending.

rows.scene: Show the auspicious birth to Aditi on Dvadashi and Shravana; the child is the manifest divine form. Keep the moment intimate.
rows.candidate_status: Producer uncertain: the infant has one face, four attached arms with four attributes, and two five-toed feet; infant face/torso patches measure B−R 75/61. Aditi cheek is R−B 99 and Kashyapa face R−B 111. Aditi’s supporting fingers partly overlap and cannot all be counted; a thin white forehead mark is visible. Final-plan independent review is pending.

rows.scene: A small distinct group of Devas showers flowers while Aditi and Kashyapa praise with joined hands; Vamana becomes a capable young brahmachari. Vamana has two arms.

reference.label: Original reference: photo 006 (both 005 and 006 map to #5)

rows.candidate_status: Producer needs-fix after the capped repairs: v011 preserves the stanza’s flower-showering Devas as two distinct figures and both casting hands show a thumb plus four fingers; both Vamana feet show five toes. Human face samples remain copper-orange (R−B 138–148); Vamana face is slate-blue (B−R 24). Final attempts v013/v014 add the cradle and tokens but omit the required Devas, so v011 is retained for its closer canonical scene. Final-plan independent review is pending.

rows.scene: Prajapatis perform Vamana’s initiation and offer sacred thread, staff, deer skin and prayer beads; after the fire rite he departs toward Bali’s Ashvamedha.
rows.candidate_status: Producer needs-fix: the initiation scene includes the fire, thread, staff, deer skin and beads; Vamana’s face is deep blue (B−R 118) and Kashyapa’s arm is muted brown (R−B 93). Brahma has four attached arms but only three heads are visible; the required fourth rear-facing head or silhouette is not visible. Final-plan independent review is pending.

rows.scene: The short brahmachari walks with umbrella and staff; the earth subtly trembles under his emerging divine gravity. Two arms, no Krishna feather or crown.
rows.candidate_status: Producer needs-fix: v009 depicts one Vamana walking with parasol and staff, ground cracks, one face, two arms, and five toes on both feet. Vamana’s face/torso remain slate blue-grey, B−R 19/20 versus the plan’s threshold of 45. Final attempt v010 deepens the blue but replaces the walking scene with Aditi, Kashyapa and Devas; v009 is retained for stanza accuracy. Final-plan independent review is pending.

rows.scene: Vamana arrives at the Hayamedha hall on the north bank of the Narmada. His presence dazzles Shukra and sages, who wonder whether he is Sun, Fire, Sanatkumara or a yogi.

reference.label: Original reference (caption/photo mismatch; canonical scene controls)

rows.candidate_status: Producer pass: Shukra and three sages are visibly distinct; no repeated sage. Human skin patches range R-B 90–108; Vamana cheek B-R 99. Both Vamana feet show five toes. Prior independent review passed this exact checksum against the earlier plan. Final-plan independent review is pending.

rows.scene: Bhrigus bring radiant Vamana to Bali’s hall. Bali welcomes him, washes both feet and receives that water reverently on his head.
rows.candidate_status: Producer pass: Bali’s basin washing and crown-receiving gesture are legible; Vamana’s feet show five toes each. Bali/sage skin R-B values are 103/101/93; Vamana B-R 84. Prior independent review passed this exact checksum against the earlier plan. Final-plan independent review is pending.

rows.scene: Canonical-only stanza: Bali’s Prahlada lineage and sacrifices explain his fortune in receiving the sacred water from the Lord’s foot, water cherished on Shiva’s head. Show Bali reverently receiving the water, with Shiva and Ganga as a restrained devotional echo.
rows.candidate_status: Producer pass: the canonical-only water stream contacts Bali’s crown before continuing to Shiva’s hair. Both visible Vamana feet show five toes; Bali skin is R−B 81 and Vamana is B−R 89. This is the no-reference stanza: no photo/caption is mapped. Final-plan independent review is pending.
